title: Mathematics on arXiv — daily notable papers, 26 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart, and citation/attention evidence is sparse or unavailable for papers only days old; this is an inferred notable-paper ordering, not a measured popularity ranking.

sections.title: The lower tail of triangle counts in sparse random graphs
sections.abstract: For Erdős–Rényi graphs with n^{-1/2} << p << 1, the authors solve the graphon variational problem for every fixed lower-tail fraction, identifying the minimizing structures and a first-order transition between homogeneous random graphs and balanced two-block models.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that every variational minimizer is constant or a balanced two-block graphon, with a first-order transition at eta_*=0.009217...; the conditioned graph is correspondingly close to an Erdős–Rényi graph or a symmetric two-block stochastic block model. (Abstract; Theorems 1.1–1.2.)
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Fixed eta in (0,1), and sparse edge probability n^{-1/2} << p << 1; conclusions describe the leading lower-tail rate and conditional structure in that asymptotic regime.
sections.unique_caveat: The result does not extend to p at or below the stated sparse threshold; the authors note that a different lower-tail mechanism applies there. The conditioned graph is described up to small cut-norm error, not an exact coupling.

sections.title: Near-critical Ising interfaces in the thermal direction: Absolute continuity with respect to SLE₃
sections.abstract: For the Ising model in the Dobrushin square at mesh delta and inverse temperature beta=beta_c-m delta with fixed nonzero m, the author proves uniformly bounded positive and negative moments of the interface likelihood ratio against critical Ising and mutual absolute continuity of every subsequential scaling limit with chordal SLE_3.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves uniform-in-mesh bounds on all positive and negative likelihood-ratio moments (and both KL divergences), then deduces that every subsequential limit is mutually absolutely continuous with SLE_3, with Radon–Nikodym derivatives in every finite L^p. (Abstract; Theorem 1.1.)
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Square-lattice Ising model with Dobrushin boundary conditions in the Dobrushin square, mesh delta=1/n, and fixed m != 0 in the thermal scaling window beta=beta_c-m delta.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper does not identify the subsequential limit uniquely or identify it as a particular massive-SLE law; the author flags uniqueness and extensions beyond the square as open directions.

sections.title: Probabilistic ultraviolet renormalization of the two-dimensional Sine-Gordon model
sections.abstract: The authors construct the two-dimensional Sine–Gordon measure by a probabilistic martingale method for every real activity and the full subcritical coupling range beta^2 in [0,4), on bounded convex domains for a broad class of log-correlated Gaussian covariances.
sections.claimed_result: Under the paper’s covariance and decomposition assumptions, normalized renormalized partition functions converge to a probability measure throughout beta^2 < 4, for all alpha in R. (Abstract; Theorem 2.3.)
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A bounded convex domain in two dimensions; a log-correlated Gaussian field with covariance K(x,y)=-log|x-y|+O(1), a bounded nonnegative density, and the paper’s white-noise-decomposition assumption; coupling remains strictly below the BKT threshold beta^2=4.
sections.unique_caveat: The critical endpoint beta^2=4 is not covered. The authors say construction of correlation functions is deferred to forthcoming work.

sections.title: A counterexample to Tokareva's conjecture on sums of two bent functions
sections.abstract: The authors disprove Tokareva’s converse conjecture by giving a degree-four Boolean function on F_2^8 that is not a sum of two bent functions, extend the counterexamples to every even dimension at least eight, and derive counterexamples to a related derivative conjecture in every even dimension at least ten.
sections.claimed_result: The authors exhibit x1x2(x3x4+x5x6+x7x8) as a non-sum of two bent functions on F_2^8, extend this construction to all even n >= 8, and use Shaporenko’s reduction for derivative-conjecture counterexamples for all even n >= 10. (Abstract.)
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Boolean functions on even-dimensional binary vector spaces; the original converse concerns functions of algebraic degree at most n/2.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors’ comment says the counterexamples and proofs arose through a large LLM-agent campaign and invites feedback on correctness, exposition, and attribution; independent mathematical verification remains important.

sections.title: Biases in gaps between zeros of Dirichlet L-functions
sections.abstract: The authors identify and classify a rare family of Dirichlet L-functions with a nonvanishing Gauss-type sum, report an experimentally observed bias in zero-gap distributions for that family, and prove that these are the only cuspidal automorphic L-functions on GL(1)/Q or GL(2)/Q whose associated Z-functions have a large integrated mean.
sections.claimed_result: The authors classify characters for which the Gauss-type sum is nonzero and derive the stated uniqueness of the automorphic families with large integrated Z-function mean. They also report a previously undetected zero-gap bias in that rare family. (Abstract.)
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Primitive Dirichlet characters and cuspidal automorphic L-functions over Q, restricted to GL(1) and GL(2); the family with the bias has density zero among primitive characters.
sections.unique_caveat: The zero-gap bias is described as experimentally observed; the abstract’s rigorous classification concerns the Gauss-type sum and the resulting mean-value statement, not a claim that the phenomenon is common.

sections.title: Sharp Projection Bounds for Intermediate Dimensions of Measures
sections.abstract: The authors prove sharp almost-everywhere and exceptional-set bounds for upper and lower intermediate dimensions under orthogonal and radial projection, and construct a measure whose projected dimension functions vary on open sets of directions.
sections.claimed_result: The authors show both dimension functions are preserved almost everywhere when the quasi-Assouad dimension is at most the target dimension, give sharp exceptional-set estimates using the source dimension function, and construct the stated open-direction variation example. (Abstract.)
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Compactly supported measures; orthogonal and radial projections; the almost-everywhere preservation statement assumes the quasi-Assouad dimension does not exceed the target dimension.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is about the specified intermediate-dimension functions and projection settings; the exceptional-set bounds depend on the source dimension function and should not be read as a universal projection theorem for arbitrary measures or dimension notions.

sections.title: Homogenization of the Stokes equations in a domain perforated by a thin truss
sections.abstract: For stationary Stokes flow through periodic domains perforated by trusses whose width shrinks faster than the period, the authors identify scaling regimes yielding effective Stokes, Brinkman, or Darcy equations and compute the effective coefficients in the Darcy and Brinkman regimes.
sections.claimed_result: The authors derive Brinkman equations in the critical regime, unchanged Stokes equations in the subcritical regime, and Darcy’s law in a subrange of the supercritical regime, with explicit coefficients for the Darcy and Brinkman limits. (Abstract.)
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Stationary Stokes equations in periodically perforated domains; truss width a_epsilon tends to zero faster than period size epsilon. The effective Darcy regime is only claimed for a subrange of the supercritical scaling.
sections.unique_caveat: The Darcy result does not cover the entire supercritical range; the abstract does not claim a universal effective law for arbitrary perforation geometries.

sections.title: Large deviations and applications in homogeneous dynamics
sections.abstract: Assuming exponential mixing, the authors prove a sub-Gaussian large-deviation estimate for smooth compactly supported test functions under a semisimple homogeneous action and apply it to effective uniqueness of the maximal-entropy measure and pointwise equidistribution on full expanding horospheres for Haar-almost every point.
sections.claimed_result: For left translation by a on finite-volume G/Gamma, with Ad(a) diagonalizable over R, the authors prove sub-Gaussian deviations under exponential mixing; they derive effective uniqueness of the maximal-entropy measure and quantitative pointwise equidistribution on each full expanding horosphere for Haar-a.e. point. (Abstract.)
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Semisimple homogeneous space of finite volume; smooth compactly supported observables; exponential mixing; real-diagonalizable adjoint action.
sections.unique_caveat: The large-deviation theorem is conditional on exponential mixing, and the equidistribution conclusion is an almost-everywhere statement rather than a claim for every point.

sections.title: Graph distance and percolation dimension of three-dimensional Brownian motion
sections.abstract: The author proves that the minimum Hausdorff dimension of a continuous path joining the endpoints within the range of three-dimensional Brownian motion is an almost-sure deterministic constant gamma_3 in (1,5/3], relates it to a graph-distance growth exponent by gamma_3=2 theta, and establishes moment-growth asymptotics.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves almost-sure existence of gamma_3, constructs continuum many simple minimizing curves with that Hausdorff and box dimension, and shows the endpoint graph distance and diameter share an exponent theta with gamma_3=2 theta. (Abstract.)
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The range of standard three-dimensional Brownian motion on [0,1]; paths join W_0 to W_1 while staying inside that random range.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract bounds gamma_3 and characterizes it through theta, but gives no explicit numerical value for either exponent.
